07-025.r: Art. 215 → High Courts are courts of record; Art. 222 → transfer of judges between High Courts; Art. 226 → writ jurisdiction; Art. 227 → superintendence over all courts.

07-026.r: Part VIII (Union Territories): Art. 239 → administration of UTs; Art. 240 → President's regulations; Art. 241 → High Courts for UTs; Art. 242 → repealed.

07-027.r: Art. 76 → Attorney General; Art. 148 → CAG; Art. 75(1) → appointment of Union Ministers; Art. 131 → original jurisdiction of Supreme Court.

07-028.r: Art. 14 → equality before law; Art. 41 → right to work; Art. 42 → just, humane work conditions; Art. 45 → now early childhood care and education below six.
07-028.c: Option (b) fits the old text. Since the 86th Amendment (2002), free and compulsory education is Article 21A and Article 45 covers early childhood care, so the book marks none.

07-029.r: Art. 371C → special provisions for Manipur, not Meghalaya; 371A → Nagaland; 371B → Assam; 371D → Andhra Pradesh.

08-001.r: 12 Schedules now; originally 8; 9th added by 1st Amendment 1951 (validation of Acts); 10th by 52nd Amendment 1985 (anti-defection).

08-003.r: Constitution originally had 22 Parts (not 20) and 395 Articles (not 390); Ninth, Tenth, Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules were added by amendments (Ninth by First Amendment, 1951).

08-004.r: First Schedule → States and Union Territories; Second → salaries of public officials, Judges, CAG; Third → oaths and affirmations; Fourth → Rajya Sabha seats.

08-005.r: Creating a new State or UT → amend the First Schedule (list of States and Union Territories).

08-006.r: Fourth Schedule → allocation of seats in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha).

08-007.r: Third Schedule → oaths for Union Ministers, Parliament candidates, MPs, Supreme Court judges, CAG, State ministers and legislators; President's oath is not in it.

08-008.r: Third Schedule → oaths and affirmations; Fourth → Rajya Sabha seats; Seventh → Union, State and Concurrent subject lists; Eighth → languages.

08-009.r: Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes → Fifth Schedule, not Sixth; Sixth → tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram; Fourth → Rajya Sabha seats; Seventh → Union List.
08-009.t: Don't confuse Fifth (Scheduled Areas) with Sixth (tribal areas of four North-East States).

08-010.r: 4th Schedule → Council of States seats; 6th → tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram; 8th → languages; 9th → land reforms.

08-011.r: 7th Schedule → distribution of legislative powers (three lists); 8th → languages; 9th → validation of certain Acts; 10th → disqualification on defection.
08-011.h: 7-8-9-10: Lists, Languages, Land laws, Leaving party (defection).

08-013.r: Allocation of Rajya Sabha seats → Fourth Schedule, not Ninth; Third → oaths; Eighth → languages; Tenth → anti-defection.

08-014.r: Ninth Schedule → added by First Amendment Act 1951, under PM Jawaharlal Nehru, to protect zamindari abolition laws.

08-015.r: State land reform and zamindari abolition laws → protected in the 9th Schedule, inserted by First Amendment, June 1951.

08-016.r: Parliament can place a law in the Ninth Schedule (true); such laws are not beyond court review, per Supreme Court ruling of 2007 (false). Entries: originally 13, now 284.

08-017.r: Coelho case ('9th Schedule case') → courts can review Ninth Schedule laws for violating the basic structure of the Constitution.

08-018.r: Three legislative lists (Union, State, Concurrent) → Seventh Schedule.

08-019.r: Original lists: Union List 97 entries (now 98); State List 66 (now 59); Concurrent List 47 (now 52).
08-019.h: Union up by one, State down by seven, Concurrent up by five.

08-020.r: Economic and Social Planning → Concurrent List, Entry 20; the Planning Commission was set up under this entry.

08-022.r: Prevention of cruelty to animals → Concurrent List (Entry 17), Seventh Schedule.

08-023.r: Criminal law (IPC, now BNS 2023) → Concurrent List; Police → State List; Foreign Affairs, Radio and Television → Union List.

08-024.r: Population control and family planning → Concurrent List (Entry 20-A, 42nd Amendment 1976); public health and sanitation, treasure trove, per-person tax → State List.

08-025.r: Concurrent List → adulteration of foodstuffs and goods (Entry 18), succession (Entry 5); inter-State trade → Union List (Entry 42); trade within State → State List (Entry 26).

08-026.r: Concurrent List → protection of wild animals and birds (Entry 17B) and price control; income on agriculture and electricity tax are not Concurrent. Parliament's law prevails in conflict.

08-027.r: Rajya Sabha seat allocation → Fourth Schedule, not Second; Public Health → State List; Census → Union List; Anti-defection → Tenth Schedule.

08-028.r: Education → moved from State List (Entry 11) to Concurrent List by 42nd Amendment, 1976; Concurrent List now has 52 subjects.

08-030.r: 42nd Amendment, 1976 → moved forests, education and protection of wild animals and birds from State List to Concurrent List.
08-030.h: 42nd moved a FEW subjects: Forests, Education, Wildlife.

08-031.r: Stock Exchange → Union List (not Concurrent); Post Office Savings Bank → Union; Public Health → State; Forest → Concurrent (originally State).

08-032.r: Census → Union List; Police and public order → State List; population control and family planning → Concurrent List; space research → residuary (with Centre).

08-033.r: Education links to all five: DPSP (Art. 45, 86th Amendment 2002), local bodies (Arts 243G, 243W), Fifth, Sixth and Seventh Schedules. Tenth Schedule → anti-defection.

08-036.r: Banking, Insurance, Census → Union List; Gas → State List.

08-037.r: Defence, Foreign Affairs, Railways → Union List; Agriculture → State List.

08-038.r: Railway Police → State List; Education, Electricity, Forest → Concurrent List.

08-039.r: Railway Police → State List (Railways → Union List); Corporation Tax, Census → Union List; Economic and Social Planning → Concurrent List.
08-039.t: Don't confuse Railways (Union List) with Railway Police (State List).

08-040.r: Local government (Panchayati Raj) → State List, Entry 5, Seventh Schedule.

08-041.r: Criminal Procedure → Concurrent List; Public Order, Prisons, Police → State List.

08-042.r: Marriage, divorce, adoption → Concurrent List (List III), Entry 5, Seventh Schedule.

08-043.r: Elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice-President → List I, Entry 72; elections to State Legislature subject to Parliament's law → List II, Entry 37.

08-044.r: Power to levy taxes and fees → Seventh Schedule (three lists); Art. 246 distributes legislative powers, including taxation, between Parliament and States.

08-045.r: Inter-State quarantine and inter-State migration → Union List, Entry 81; inter-State trade and commerce → Union List, Entry 42; corporation tax is not a State subject.

08-046.r: Land reforms → State List; land reform Acts protected by the Ninth Schedule, added by 1st Amendment Act, 1951.

08-047.r: Anti-defection law → Tenth Schedule, added by 52nd Amendment Act, 1985; lays down disqualification of legislators on grounds of defection.

08-049.r: Fifth Schedule (Scheduled Areas and Tribes) → Samatha vs State of Andhra Pradesh, 1997: transfer of tribal land to private parties for mining is void.

08-050.r: Area under Fifth Schedule → transfer of tribal land to non-tribals can be prevented; President declares scheduled areas (10 States have them); Governor can amend regulations.

08-051.r: Fifth Schedule → administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in all States except Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

08-052.r: Fifth Schedule → Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes, except in Assam, Tripura, Meghalaya, Mizoram, whose tribal areas fall under the Sixth Schedule.
08-052.t: Don't confuse Fifth (Scheduled Areas, several States) with Sixth (tribal areas of four North-East States).

08-053.r: Fifth and Sixth Schedules → special provisions to protect the interests of Scheduled Tribes.

08-054.r: Sixth Schedule → tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram (through Arts 244(2), 275(1)); aim: preserve tribal culture.

08-055.r: Sixth Schedule covers Assam, Tripura, Meghalaya and Mizoram; Manipur is not covered.
08-055.t: Manipur is a North-East State but not a Sixth Schedule State.

08-058.r: Scheduled Areas → notified by President's order (Art. 244(1)); States with them must set up a Tribal Advisory Council (para 4, Fifth Schedule).

08-059.r: Scheduled Area is notified by President's order (true); largest unit is the district, lowest a cluster of villages in a block (true); the Chief Ministers statement is false.

08-060.r: Fifth Schedule area: State keeps its executive power there (no local body takeover); Union cannot take over its administration on Governor's recommendation; both statements false.

08-061.r: Sixth Schedule Autonomous District Council: 30 members (true); Governor directs how Parliament's Acts apply in Assam's autonomous districts (true); '24 elected, 6 nominated' is false.

08-062.r: Eleventh Schedule → Panchayati Raj; added by 73rd Amendment, 1992; 29 subjects.
08-062.h: Panchayat trio: 73rd Amendment, Eleventh Schedule, 29 subjects.

08-063.r: Powers and responsibilities of Panchayats → Eleventh Schedule (Art. 243G), added by 73rd Amendment Act 1992; 29 entries.

09-001.r: Preamble gives the adoption date → 'this twenty-sixth day of November, 1949'.

09-002.r: On 26 January 1950 India was 'A Sovereign Democratic Republic'; 'socialist', 'secular' and 'integrity' were added by 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.

09-004.r: Preamble reflects the mind of the Constitution's makers; K.M. Munshi called it the political horoscope.

09-006.r: Preamble: 3 types of justice, 5 of liberty, 2 of equality, 1 fraternity → 3, 5, 2, 1.
09-006.h: Justice: social, economic, political (3); Liberty: thought, expression, belief, faith, worship (5); Equality: status, opportunity (2).

09-007.r: Preamble order: Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic (as amended by 42nd Amendment, 1976); word 'People's' is not in it (it is in China's Constitution).
09-007.h: Three S's, then D, then R: SSS-D-R.

09-008.r: 42nd Amendment inserted 'Socialist' and 'Secular' into the Preamble; 'Sovereign' and 'Republic' were already in the original Preamble.

09-009.r: Preamble order: Sovereign → Socialist → Secular → Democratic → Republic; then Justice, Liberty, Equality, Fraternity.

09-012.r: 'Socialist' → added to the Preamble by 42nd Amendment Act (1976), along with 'secular' and 'integrity'.

09-015.r: 42nd Amendment Act 1976 (on Swaran Singh Committee's advice) → added 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.

09-016.r: Preamble describes India as a Secular State; 'Secular' was added by 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.

09-017.r: 'Integrity' was not in the Preamble in 1975; added in 1976 by 42nd Amendment; Fraternity, Sovereign, Equality were original words.

09-019.r: Preamble: grew from Nehru's Objectives Resolution; non-justiciable; can be amended (Kesavananda Bharati, 1973); cannot override specific provisions of the Constitution.

09-021.r: 42nd Amendment, 1976 changed the Preamble: 'Sovereign Democratic Republic' → 'Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic'; 'unity of the Nation' → 'unity and integrity of the Nation'.

09-022.r: Original Preamble (26 November 1949): Sovereign, Democratic, Republic. 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' added by 42nd Amendment, 1976; 'Reliable', 'Non-religious' never in it.

09-027.r: Preamble secures: Justice (social, economic, political); Liberty (thought, expression, belief, faith, worship); Equality (status, opportunity); Fraternity (dignity of individual, unity and integrity).

09-028.r: 'Sovereign socialist secular democratic republic' was substituted for 'Sovereign Democratic Republic' by 42nd Amendment Act 1976, the only Preamble amendment so far; A and R true.

09-029.r: 'We, the People of India' (opening words of the Preamble) → people's sovereignty: India is governed by its Constitution, not by any external power.

09-031.r: 'All individuals are fully and equally human' → Universalism: everyone is entitled to human rights without discrimination.

09-032.r: Secular in India → no official religion of the State; State treats all religions equally (positive secularism).

09-033.r: 'Federal' is not in the Preamble; it has Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic.

09-034.r: 'Public Welfare' is not in the Preamble; Socialist, Secular and Sovereign are.

09-035.r: Preamble liberty → thought, expression, belief, faith and worship; economic liberty is not included.

09-036.r: Preamble justice → social, economic, political; 'religious justice' is not mentioned.

09-037.r: 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were not in the Preamble when the Constitution came into force in 1950; inserted by 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 (not 1977 or 1985).

09-038.r: Preamble → 'Soul of the Constitution'; K.M. Munshi called it the 'horoscope of our sovereign democratic republic'.

09-040.r: B.R. Ambedkar → held that the Constitution must be treated as a basic and sacred document; chaired the Drafting Committee from 1947.

09-041.r: Berubari case (1960) → Supreme Court first held that the Preamble is not an integral part of the Constitution.

09-042.r: S.R. Bommai vs Union of India (1994) → Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution; Kesavananda Bharati (1973, 13 judges) → Basic Structure doctrine.

09-043.r: Kesavananda Bharati case → Supreme Court treated the Preamble as part of the basic structure of the Constitution.

09-044.r: Preamble's ideals are elaborated in Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles and Fundamental Duties; the Preamble reflects the Constitution's objectives.

09-046.r: Preamble → 3 types of justice: social, economic and political.

09-048.r: Economic Justice → in the Preamble and in DPSP (e.g. Art. 38(1): a social order with social, economic and political justice).

09-049.r: Preamble → part of the Constitution (Kesavananda Bharati, 1973) but not enforceable in court; it has no legal effect on its own.

09-050.r: Preamble: not enforceable in courts, important and useful, states aims of governance, aids judicial interpretation; amended only once, 1976 (42nd Amendment).
09-050.c: No answer printed: explanation says all four statements are correct, but no option lists 1, 2, 3 and 4.

09-051.r: Social equality is guaranteed by the Constitution → Right to Equality, Arts 14-18; the Preamble also aims at it.

10-001.r: State (Garner) → community of people permanently occupying a definite territory, independent of external control, with an organised government the people obey.

10-002.r: Four elements of a State: population, territory, government, sovereignty; sovereignty is the most important (pre-1947 India lacked it).

10-003.r: India is a Commonwealth member and accepts the British Crown as Commonwealth head (1947 declaration), but this extra-constitutional step does not curtail its sovereignty.

10-004.r: Idea of the Preamble → from the US Constitution; its language → from the Australian Constitution.
10-004.t: Don't confuse the idea (USA) with the language (Australia).

10-005.r: Indian Constitution → Parliamentary form of government, modelled on the UK; executive draws legitimacy from and is accountable to the legislature.

10-006.r: In a Parliamentary system, the Legislature controls the Executive.

10-007.r: Parliamentary (Cabinet) system → Government drawn from and responsible to Parliament; stays in power only while it has majority support in the popular house.

10-008.r: Parliamentary form of government first emerged in Great Britain (UK).

10-009.r: India's parliamentary system differs from Britain's by having judicial review (from US Constitution); real and nominal executive, collective responsibility, bicameralism are common to both.

10-010.r: British Parliament is sovereign; Indian Parliament's law-making power is limited, and constitutionality of amendments goes to a Supreme Court Constitution Bench. Both statements true.

10-011.r: Indian Constitution features: Parliamentary government, independent judiciary, federal government; Presidential government is not a feature.

10-012.r: India has Parliamentary, not Presidential, government: President is nominal head; real executive is Council of Ministers under PM; India is secular and federal.

10-013.r: India is Parliamentary because the executive (Council of Ministers under PM) is collectively responsible to the legislature, mainly Lok Sabha (Art. 75(3)); A and R true, R explains A.

10-014.r: India has a Parliamentary system because the Council of Ministers is responsible to the Lok Sabha; executive members come from the legislature.

10-015.r: Main advantage of Parliamentary government → the executive stays responsible to the legislature, giving a responsible government.

10-016.r: Parliamentary government implies: Cabinet members are MPs; ministers stay while they enjoy Parliament's confidence; Cabinet is not headed by Head of State. Non-MP minister goes after six months (Art. 75(5)).

10-017.r: Parliamentary government: executive responsible to legislature, majority rule, collective responsibility, nominal and real executives, double membership, PM's leadership, dissolution of lower house.

10-018.r: Cabinet form (responsible government) → mechanism of parliamentary democracy ensuring collective responsibility of the Government to the people.

10-019.r: Presidential government → all executive powers vest in the President, who is both head of State and head of Government.

10-020.r: Indian political system: democratic republic, parliamentary government, supreme power with the people; no unified authority, as powers are separated between Union and States.

10-021.r: India is a democratic polity, a sovereign state, a democratic society and (through DPSP) a welfare state; all four true.

10-022.r: Indian polity: government following the Constitution, democratic government, rule of law; authoritarian government is not a feature.

10-023.r: Central and State governments both get their authority from the Constitution, which sets up the parliamentary (Westminster) system at Centre and in States.

10-024.r: India is democratic and has its own written Constitution, but a constitution does not make a country democratic (UK is democratic without one); A and R true, R not explanation.

10-025.r: Good governance features: accountability, transparency, rule of law; red tapism (excess regulation blocking action) is not one.

10-026.r: Welfare State → State protects and promotes citizens' social and economic well-being, especially weaker sections; based on equal opportunity and fair distribution of wealth.

10-027.r: 'The State is everywhere: it leaves hardly a gap' → describes the Welfare State.

10-028.r: Constitution's philosophy (Preamble): welfare state, socialist state, political equality through adult franchise; a Communist State is not part of it.

10-029.r: India is a Parliamentary Democracy, not presidential, not a titular monarchy, not an aristocracy.

10-030.r: Main source of political power in India → the People ('We the People of India'); India is a democratic republic.

10-031.r: Basic feature of Presidential government → single executive (power centralised in the President).

10-032.r: Presidential government: President heads State and executive, appoints his Council of Ministers, cannot dissolve the legislature → all three true.

10-033.r: Presidential government first formed in the USA (oldest, purest form); President elected indirectly by the people for a fixed term.

10-034.r: Indian democracy rests on the people's right to choose and change the Government through elections.

10-035.r: Democracy's superior virtue → it calls into activity the intelligence and character of ordinary men and women.

10-036.r: 'India is a Republic' → no hereditary ruler; Head of State (President) is elected, indirectly, through people's representatives.

10-038.r: Distribution of powers between Union and States makes the Constitution federal; in a unitary constitution all power lies with a central authority.

10-039.r: Indian Constitution → partly rigid, partly flexible: some parts amended by simple majority, some by two-thirds (Art. 368), some also need ratification by 50% of States.

10-040.r: Indian vs British system: India has judicial review, as Indian Parliament is subject to the Constitution; British Parliament is sovereign (no written constitution).

10-041.r: Constitution gives a federal system and a very strong Centre (A, R true, R not explanation); Ambedkar: federal in normal times, unitary in war or Emergency.

10-042.r: Federalism is not fully practical in India (A true), but India is a federal state with divided powers (R false): federal in nature, unitary in spirit; Wheare: quasi-federal.

10-043.r: Independence of the judiciary → essential federal feature, since the judiciary interprets the Constitution.

10-044.r: Single citizenship is a unitary, not federal, feature; federal features: written and rigid Constitution, division of powers, independent judiciary, bicameral legislature.
10-044.t: Single citizenship, Governors appointed by President and Emergency powers are unitary features.

10-045.r: Unitary elements in Indian federation: appointment of Governor, President's approval of State bills, constitutional crisis (emergency); written, rigid, supreme Constitution are federal features.

10-046.r: Unitary elements: appointment of Governors, unequal representation in Rajya Sabha, All India Services (also strong Centre, single citizenship).

10-047.r: Federal system is the basic structure (Seventh Schedule, Arts 245-255) with a strong unitary bias (true); Union and State legislatures are not both sovereign; statements 3 and 4 false.

10-048.r: Unitary government: swift decisions, flexibility, uniform laws; not 'ideal for large countries'. Its traits: strong Centre, single citizenship, integrated judiciary, All-India Services.

10-049.r: President of India is elected indirectly because the parliamentary system is combined with republicanism (no hereditary Head of State); A and R true, R explains A.

10-050.r: Political parties are the life-blood of democracy (they form governments, shape policies); people blame them for bad governance; book: both true, R explains A.

10-051.r: Party-less democracy → supported by both Mahatma Gandhi and Jayaprakash Narayan.

10-052.r: India's federal design aims to weave a nation from diverse parts and protect integration; accommodating diversity made nationhood stronger; A, R true, R explains A.

10-053.r: Indian political system shows 'continuity and change': it mixes modern, traditional and saintly styles from Mauryan times on; A, R true, R explains A.

10-054.r: Women, Dalits, poor and minorities → biggest stakeholders of Indian democracy, which carries their desire for self-respect; A, R true, R explains A.

10-055.r: Constitution is the world's longest written one; reasons: many constitutions' experience, detailed administrative provisions, large country, Union and State constitutions together.
10-055.c: No answer printed: book says all four options are true reasons, so no single option is correct.

10-056.r: USA → federal government (federal republic of 50 States); India → Union of 28 States and 8 UTs (Art. 1).

10-057.r: Indian federalism is not the result of an agreement among federating units; its features: written Constitution, divided powers, independent judiciary, unequal Rajya Sabha representation.
